title: A Shared Representation of the Space Near Oneself and Others in the Human Premotor Cortex

findings.antecedent: visual stimulus (moving ball) presented near real hands (participant's own and another person's) vs. near participant's own hand and a prosthetic hand
findings.consequent: BOLD adaptation in left ventral premotor (PMv)
findings.mechanism: neuronal populations that encode the space both around the participant's and another person's hand
findings.quote: stronger BOLD adaptation to the moving object presented near the real rather than the artificial hand following stimulation near the participant's own hand.

findings.antecedent: visual stimulus (moving ball) presented near real hands (participant's own and another person's) vs. near participant's own hand and a prosthetic hand
findings.mechanism: shared neuronal representation of perihand space

findings.antecedent: visual stimulus (moving ball) presented near real hands (participant's own and another person's) vs. near participant's own hand and a prosthetic hand
findings.consequent: BOLD adaptation in right anterior cingulate gyrus
findings.mechanism: shared neuronal representation of perihand space

findings.antecedent: visual stimulus (moving ball) presented near other person's hand in left hemispace
findings.mechanism: neuronal populations in the left PMv encode the physical stimulus near... the other person's hand irrespective of whether the other's hand was located in the left... or the right hemispace
findings.quote: irrespective of whether the other's hand was located in the left (T = 3.25, p < 0.001 uncorrected)

findings.antecedent: visual stimulus (moving ball) presented near other person's hand in right hemispace
findings.mechanism: neuronal populations in the left PMv encode the physical stimulus near... the other person's hand irrespective of whether the other's hand was located in the left... or the right hemispace
findings.quote: irrespective of whether the other's hand was located in the... right hemispace (T = 3.63, PFWE-corrected = 0.045; Figure 2A).

findings.antecedent: visual stimulation near participant's hand followed by stimulation near other person's hand (Self-Other sequence) OR stimulation near other person's hand followed by stimulation near participant's hand (Other-Self sequence)
findings.consequent: bidirectional BOLD adaptation in left PMv
findings.mechanism: the same neuronal population responds indifferently to an object near the participant's and the other person's hand
findings.quote: the left PMv adapted to the visual simulation near the participant's hand and the other person's hand independently of the order of presentation to the two hands (peak in the inferior part of the precentral sulcus; T = 3.77, PFWE-corrected = 0.016; Figure 2B; Table 2)

findings.antecedent: visual stimulation near participant's hand followed by stimulation near other person's hand (SbO versus OaS contrast)
findings.mechanism: voxels showing significant adaptation when stimulation near one's own hand follows or precedes stimulation near the other person's hand
findings.quote: SbO versus OaS: p = 0.016, T = 3.77 in [42, 2; 24]

findings.antecedent: visual stimulation near other person's hand followed by stimulation near participant's hand (ObS versus SaO contrast)
findings.mechanism: voxels showing significant adaptation when stimulation near one's own hand follows or precedes stimulation near the other person's hand
findings.quote: ObS versus SaO: p = 0.035, T = 3.56 in [-40; 4; 24]

findings.antecedent: visual stimulation near participant's hand followed by stimulation near other person's hand (Self-Other sequence) OR stimulation near other person's hand followed by stimulation near participant's hand (Other-Self sequence)
findings.consequent: bidirectional BOLD adaptation in left inferior temporal gyrus

findings.antecedent: visual stimulus (moving ball) presented near another individual's hand vs. near participant's own hand
findings.consequent: BOLD adaptation in right anterior cingulate cortex (ACC)
findings.mechanism: ACC might use the shared premotor peripersonal space to support higher-level representations of interacting individuals
findings.quote: the right anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) showed greater selectivity for the space near another individual's hand compared to one's own hand (T = 3.73, PFWE-corrected = 0.047; Figure S3; Table S2).

stimuli.description: a small red ball (3 cm diameter) attached to a stick moved repeatedly up and down, 2 cm above the fingers, near participant's own hand, another person's hand, or a prosthetic hand.

tables.description: MNI coordinates, peak t-value, and peak p-value for brain regions showing stronger BOLD adaptation to repeated perihand visual stimulation between self and other than between self and the prosthetic hand (Experiment 1).
key_stats: Left inferior precentral sulcus (PMv): T=3.95, p=0.015
Right anterior cingulate gyrus: T=3.66, p=0.001

tables.description: MNI coordinates, peak t-value, and peak p-value for brain regions showing bidirectional BOLD adaptation between self and other (Experiment 2).
key_stats: Left inferior precentral sulcus (PMv): T=3.77, p=0.016
Left inferior temporal gyrus: T=5.13, p=0.036
